instruction: Please write Rego code that enforces the SLSA Provenance Attestation format for RHTAP Multi-CI builds
input:
REQUIREMENTS:
Develop a deny rule that validates the attestation structure created by the RHTAP Multi-CI pipeline, ensuring it conforms to expected SLSA Provenance standards with the package name rhtap_multi_ci

ATTESTATION_SCHEMA:
- (None - validates rule data format only)

AVAILABLE_HELPERS:
- name: lib.json
- name: j.validate_schema
  signature: # Validates schema reporting the error message as well as the severity
validate_schema if {
  description: Validates schema reporting the error message as well as the severity
- name: lib.result_helper
  signature: result_helper(chain, terms)
  usage: `result := lib.result_helper(rego.metadata.chain(), [task.name])`
  description: Creates violation result with metadata from chain and terms for message formatting
- name: rego.metadata.chain()
  description: Returns metadata chain for current rule

NAVIGATION_HINTS:
- Result output: `result := lib.result_helper(rego.metadata.chain(), [terms])`

SUGGESTED_PACKAGE: rhtap_multi_ci
SUGGESTED_RULE_TYPE: deny
output:
ANALYSIS:
- The rule accesses **attestations** from the input data, specifically filtering for SLSA provenance attestations of version **v1.0** and build types associated with RHTAP Multi-CI pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub, GitLab, Azure).
- It iterates over the filtered attestations to validate that each matches the expected **JSON schema** for the build type, ensuring required fields like `runDetails`, `builder.id`, and `metadata.invocationID` are present and correctly structured.
- The core validation logic triggers a violation if an attestation does not conform to the expected schema for its build type, particularly checking for missing or malformed fields in the `predicate` section of the SLSA statement.
- The result is generated as a **deny rule** that fails when any attestation does not meet the format requirements, with a failure message indicating the specific build type and validation issue.
- The rule uses a **schema-based validation approach** with a base schema patched per CI type to ensure compliance with expected attestation formats.

RULE:
```rego
package rhtap_multi_ci

import rego.v1
import data.lib
import data.lib.json as j

_all_attestations := input.attestations

_attestations := [att |
	some att in _all_attestations

	# Beware we are not supporting SLSA formats other than v1.0 here
	att.statement.predicateType == _slsa_provenance_predicate_type_v1

	# Just the RHTAP Multi-CI build types
	some known_build_type in _known_build_types
	att.statement.predicate.buildDefinition.buildType == known_build_type
]

_build_type(ci_type) := sprintf("https://redhat.com/rhtap/slsa-build-types/%s-build/v1", [ci_type])

_known_build_types := [_build_type(known_ci_type) | some known_ci_type in _known_ci_types]

_known_ci_types := ["jenkins", "github", "gitlab", "azure"]

_predicate_schema("gitlab") := json.patch(_predicate_schema_base, [])

_predicate_schema_base := {
	"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
	"type": "object",
	"required": ["runDetails"],
	"properties": {"runDetails": {
		"type": "object",
		"required": ["builder", "metadata"],
		"properties": {
			"metadata": {
				"type": "object",
				"required": ["invocationID"],
				"properties": {"invocationID": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}},
			},
			"builder": {
				"type": "object",
				"required": ["id"],
				"properties": {"id": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}},
			},
		},
	}},
}

_slsa_provenance_predicate_type_v1 := "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1"

# METADATA
# title: SLSA Provenance Attestation Format
# description: >-
#   Confirm the attestation created by the RHTAP Multi-CI build pipeline matches the
#   expected format.
# custom:
#   short_name: attestation_format
#   failure_msg: "RHTAP %s attestation problem: %s"
#   solution: >-
#     This check looks for some fields expected to be present in the SLSA attestation. Modifying
#     the scripts that produce the attestation predicate might cause this to fail. See also
#     the `att-predicate-*.sh` scripts at https://github.com/redhat-appstudio/tssc-dev-multi-ci/tree/main/rhtap
#   collections:
#   - rhtap-multi-ci
#   # For compatibility. These will be removed these soon.
#   - rhtap-github
#   - rhtap-gitlab
#   - rhtap-jenkins
#   depends_on:
#   - rhtap_multi_ci.attestation_found
#
deny contains result if {
	some att in _attestations
	some ci_type in _known_ci_types
	att.statement.predicate.buildDefinition.buildType == _build_type(ci_type)
	some schema_error in j.validate_schema(att.statement.predicate, _predicate_schema(ci_type))
	result := lib.result_helper(rego.metadata.chain(), [ci_type, schema_error.message])
}
```

```rego
package rhtap_multi_ci_test

import rego.v1

test_atts_happy_path if {
	lib.assert_empty(rhtap_multi_ci.deny) with input.attestations as [good_att]
	lib.assert_empty(rhtap_multi_ci.deny) with input.attestations as [ignored_att, good_att]
}

test_atts_missing if {
	expected := {
		"code": "rhtap_multi_ci.attestation_found",
		"msg": sprintf("%s%s%s%s%s", [
			"A SLSA v1.0 provenance with one of the following RHTAP Multi-CI build types was not found:",
			" 'https://redhat.com/rhtap/slsa-build-types/jenkins-build/v1',",
			" 'https://redhat.com/rhtap/slsa-build-types/github-build/v1',",
			" 'https://redhat.com/rhtap/slsa-build-types/gitlab-build/v1',",
			" 'https://redhat.com/rhtap/slsa-build-types/azure-build/v1'.",
		]),
	}

	lib.assert_equal_results({expected}, rhtap_multi_ci.deny) with input.attestations as []
	lib.assert_equal_results({expected}, rhtap_multi_ci.deny) with input.attestations as [ignored_att]
}

test_fields_missing if {
	expected = {
		{
			"code": "rhtap_multi_ci.attestation_format",
			"msg": "RHTAP jenkins attestation problem: runDetails.metadata: invocationID is required",
		},
		{
			"code": "rhtap_multi_ci.attestation_format",
			"msg": "RHTAP jenkins attestation problem: runDetails.builder: id is required",
		},
	}
	lib.assert_equal_results(expected, rhtap_multi_ci.deny) with input.attestations as [missing_fields_att]
}

```

_REPOSITORY := {"id": 5, "name": "GitHub Workflow Repository"}

_certs contains cert if {
	some sig in input.image.signatures

	cert.KeyUsage == 1
	cert.ExtKeyUsage == [3]

_check_extension(chain, key, extension) := result if {
	value := _fulcio_extension_value(extension)
	allowed := lib.rule_data(key)
	count(allowed) > 0
	not value in allowed
	result := lib.result_helper(chain, [value, allowed])

	id := [1, 3, 6, 1, 4, 1, 57264, 1, ext.id]
	some cert in _certs
	some extension in cert.Extensions
	extension.Id == id
	value := base64.decode(extension.Value)

  - predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].ref.name
  - predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].ref.kind
  - predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].ref.bundle
- .statement.predicate.buildConfig.tasks[]
  example: {"name": "build-container", "status": "Succeeded", "ref": {"bundle": "..."}, "results": [...]}
  navigation: `some task in tekton.tasks(att)`
  - predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].name
  - predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].ref
  - predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].results[]
  - predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].results[].name

- name: lib.image
- name: lib.tekton
- name: tekton.task_ref
  signature: task_ref(task)
  usage: `ref := tekton.task_ref(task)`
  description: Returns the task reference (bundle, name, kind)
- name: tekton.untagged_task_references
  signature: # Returns a subset of tasks that use untagged bundle Task references.
untagged_task_references(tasks
  description: Returns a subset of tasks that use untagged bundle Task references.
- name: lib.tasks_from_pipelinerun
  signature: tasks_from_pipelinerun := [ ... ]
- name: lib.result_helper_with_term
  signature: result_helper_with_term(chain, terms, term)
  usage: `result := lib.result_helper_with_term(rego.metadata.chain(), [name], name)`
  description: Creates result with an additional searchable term field

  signature: # returns a slsav0.2 pipeline task name the name field (which is the taskRun name) for slsav1.0 is m
  description: returns a slsav0.2 pipeline task name the name field (which is the taskRun name) for slsav1.0 is metadata.name
- name: tekton.task_name
  signature: # task name from a v0.2 and v1.0 attestation
task_name(task) := task_ref(task).name
  description: task name from a v0.2 and v1.0 attestation
- name: rego.metadata.chain()
  description: Returns metadata chain for current rule

NAVIGATION_HINTS:
- Task ref access: `ref := tekton.task_ref(task)`
- Result output: `result := lib.result_helper_with_term(chain, [terms], term)`
